title: dedicated gpu pool autoscale incident breadcrumbs
content:
High level:
- Breadcrumbs from the dedicated GPU pool capacity thrash incident (observed 2025-01-17 02:10-03:40 UTC).
- Purpose: capture commands I ran, error snippets, ad-hoc hypotheses, quick checks for follow-up.

Timeline (rough):
- 02:05 UTC: Customer load spike -> 2x sustained qps for ~15m.
- 02:10 UTC: Pool-controller triggered scaling: request +4 nodes (gpu-type-v100).
- 02:12 UTC: New nodes register, but pods keep restarting / Pending because warmup not complete.
- 02:18 UTC: Another scaling decision by autoscaler to add +6 (observed race between scale decisions).
- 02:25-02:40 UTC: Nodes flapping, pods evicted due to node pressure/oom or image-pull delays -> became capacity thrash.
- 02:45 UTC: Manual intervention: scaled min-capacity up in console to stabilize.

Environment notes:
- k8s cluster: redwood-prod-gpu-cluster (k8s v1.23)
- Autoscaler components: pool-controller (custom), cluster-autoscaler (forked), warmup-sidecar (image-cache), node-launcher (cloud infra).
- GPU instance type: gpu-pool-v100 (custom AMI with CUDA 11.4).

Commands / queries I ran (copy/paste):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide -l nodepool=dedicated-gpu -n kube-system
- kubectl describe pod redwood-infer-abc-zzz -n inference | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl logs -n kube-system pool-controller-77f6f6f6 -c controller | tail -n 200
- kubectl logs -n kube-system cluster-autoscaler-xxxx | grep -i 'scale' -n
- aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Pool,Values=dedicated-gpu" --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Id:InstanceId,State:State.Name,LaunchTime:LaunchTime,ImageId:ImageId}'
- ssh ubuntu@node-ip 'dmesg | tail -n 80' (checked OOM / GPU driver errors)
- curl -sS http://node-ip:10255/metrics | grep -i cuda

Observed snippets (from logs):
- pool-controller: "Requested scale up +4 -> provisioning started (request id ef7d)"
- cluster-autoscaler: "Need to scale up: insufficient pods: 12, scale up candidates: 3"
- kubelet on new node: "Failed to start container: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = couldn't create container: container create failed: ImagePullBackOff"
- kubelet dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (11)" (GPU driver reset observed on 2 new nodes)
- pod events: "Back-off restarting failed container" then "Evicted: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage"
- warmup-sidecar: "warmup cache miss: model v2.1 largest shard not present; starting download (size=12.4GB)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Warmup latency cascades -> new nodes take long to finish image/model download + warmup (12GB model), so pods show ready=false and autoscaler sees unschedulable pods -> triggers more scale-ups. New nodes register but are not yet useful. Net effect: overprovision and thrash. Evidence: warmup logs, large model shard downloads.
2) ImagePullBackOff / network egress throttling during concurrent pulls across many nodes. Evidence: ImagePullBackOff events and slower S3 download rates (observed spikes in egress metrics).
3) GPU driver instability on AMI causing NVRM errors -> node becomes unusable after driver reset and pods get evicted -> autoscaler retries. Evidence: NVRM Xid in dmesg on 2 nodes.
4) Autoscaler controller misconfiguration: aggressive scale up policy + short stabilization window -> multiple overlapping scale decisions. Evidence: pool-controller logs show overlapping request ids (ef7d, ef8a) for same pool.
5) Disk/ephemeral-storage constraints on instance type (init containers write cache during model unpack) -> evictions. Evidence: Evicted events referencing ephemeral-storage.

Quick checks to reproduce/validate:
- Trigger single node launch, watch warmup logs in isolation to measure time to model-download+warmup (goal < 90s).
- Simulate concurrent N node launches (N=5) to watch S3 throughput and ImagePullBackOff likelihood.
- Spin up same AMI in staging and run gpu stress + warmup to see NVRM replicability.
- Check cloud-side metrics for egress throttling / registry (ECR) throttling.

Commands to reproduce single-node warmup locally (staging):
- kubectl apply -f staging/dedicated-pool-test.yaml -n staging
- kubectl get pods -w -n staging --selector=app=warmup-tester
- kubectl logs warmup-tester-xxx -c warmup-sidecar -n staging --follow

Mitigations applied (short-term):
- Increased min-replicas for dedicated-gpu pool from 2 -> 6 at 02:50 UTC to reduce re-scaling churn. (manual console)
- Added temporary 600s stabilization window on pool-controller scale decisions.
- Disabled concurrent bulk-launch for 10m (rate limit new-launches).

Longer-term / action items (owners):
- Add model pre-warm cache layer at node-launch time so model shards are pre-fetched to AMI image or a shared cache (Owner: Jia Li).
- Harden AMI GPU driver: reproduce NVRM in staging, upgrade driver, bake new AMI (Owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Tune autoscaler: increase stabilization window, add warmup-aware scheduling signal (Owner: eng-serving-runtime team).
- Improve observability: add metric for "node warmup progress" and surface in console; add S3/ECR throttling alarms (Owner: Observability team).
- Add best-practice doc: recommended min pool size per model size and per expected burst (Owner: Samir Desai).

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- Why did cluster-autoscaler think there were only 3 scale-up candidates while pool-controller requested +4? check candidate selection logic.
- Confirm whether any underlying cloud rate limits were hit (ECR/S3) during 02:10-02:30. Ask infra/billing for account-level throttling logs.
- Should we pre-bake the largest models into a dedicated AMI for hot paths? cost tradeoffs.

Notes to self: keep this doc as ephemeral breadcrumbs. Merge important items into ENG SERVING RUNTIME confluence follow-up and create a JIRA epic (JIRA-ENG-2178) for warmup work.

Raw snippets (copied):
- "E013/Warmup: starting download shard-3 (http s3://models/..../shard-3.tar) latency=23.3s"
- "ImagePullBackOff: Back-off pulling image "registry.redwood/infer-sidecar:stable""
- "PoolController: scale request ef7d accepted -> pending provisioning"
- "dmesg: NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:03:00: GPU has fallen off the bus."

If you pick this up: first check warmup logs and node metrics (disk, egress, driver errors). Then follow action items.

-- Samir
